text:
Derek: heads-up - ran a short perf sweep on Mixtral-8B (MQA) focused on KV layout and kernel selection, and hit a ~12% throughput regression when we enabled paged-KV with default compaction. attaching quick notes.
Alice: can you drop the raw numbers?
Derek: sure, pasted below. testbed = 4xA100, seq distribution skewed (p95=1536), batcher = dynamic-adaptive. workload = chat-like bursty prefixes.
Carmen: interesting, I thought paged-KV was supposed to reduce memory pressure not hurt throughput.
Derek: same expectation. profiling shows fragmentation + PCIe thrash during cache compaction windows. KV occupancy grows, compaction triggers, we copy many small pages -> spikes in memcpy and kernel-switching.
Sam: do you have perf counters? L2/DRAM breakdown?
Derek: yep:
```
# hot counters (sample window)
L2_read_bandwidth: 420 GB/s -> baseline 480
DRAM_reads: +18%
PCIe_write_bytes: +60%
sm_efficiency: -6%
```
Alice: ugh pci thrash. any idea which kernel path is amplifying this? fused-mha vs tiled?
Derek: that's the other part. The runtime was selecting the fused-mha kernel for Mixtral's head_dim=128 path. For paged-KV layout, the memory access pattern for KV slot compaction leads to many non-coalesced accesses, which penalizes the fused path. switching to the tiled-kernel (more robust for scattered loads) recovered ~18% throughput in the same run.
Carmen: so kernel selection heuristic mispredicted because it only looks at model shapes and seq len, not KV fragmentation score.
Derek: exactly. proposing we add a cheap KV-fragmentation metric to kernel selector: fraction_of_small_pages + avg_slots_per_page. if > thresh, bias towards tiled-kernel.
Sam: also worth tuning num_key_value_heads? I remember Mixtral uses MQA-like split and we might be seeing head-dim mismatch causing extra memcpy for packing.
Derek: tested that too. reducing num_key_value_heads from 64->32 (keeping total kv_dim constant) lowered number of small pages and compaction frequency, improving throughput by ~6% but increased per-token compute slightly. tradeoff depends on latency SLO.
Alice: can you share minimal config diff to reproduce?
Derek: paste: 
```
# runtime config snippet
kv_layout: paged
kv_page_size: 64kb
kv_compact_threshold: 0.7  # fraction small pages
kernel_selector: auto
kernel_selector.overrides: {"fragmentation_bias": true}
num_key_value_heads: 32
```
Carmen: good. also, RoPE scaling tests? did you see any head-dim effect from RoPE scaling on Qwen vs Mixtral shapes?
Derek: yes - Qwen-like models with larger rotary base had slightly different sequence-length cache hit patterns; RoPE scaling affects per-head key correlation which changes effective reuse, so cache hotness shifts. in practice RoPE scaling made paged layout less efficient for very long prefixes (p99), because cached entries were less reused across tokens -> higher fragmentation.
Sam: so combined action items: 1) add frag metric to kernel selector, 2) expose kv_compact_threshold and recommend different defaults for MQA vs GQA, 3) document num_key_value_heads knob tradeoffs and autosuggest based on seq-dist.
Derek: adding 4) benchmark job with tiled vs fused kernel baseline across Llama/Mixtral/Qwen on same seq distribution. I started a run: infra-bot has queued job id r-bench-1832.
infra-bot: benchmark r-bench-1832 queued on 4xA100, expected duration 45m. logs -> /bench/logs/r-bench-1832.log
Alice: thanks. when we have logs let's also check per-GPU memcpy stall times and host->device queue length. those looked hairy in your trace.
Derek: will post full flamegraphs when the run completes. early takeaways: paged-KV wins memory but we must avoid small-page fragmentation; kernel heuristics need a cheap view of KV layout; num_key_value_heads is a useful lever for throughput vs latency.
Carmen: +1 on adding autosuggest. also note to PMs: this may need a default toggle for Dedicated customers to avoid surprise regressions. :warning:
Sam: filed PERF-312 to track. I'll add a unit/regression test that simulates high-fragmentation sequences.
Derek: perfect. I'll follow up with the bench logs and a short PR for the selector change. :thumbsup:
